questions.q: Four distinct points $( 2k, 3k ) , ( 1, 0 ) , ( 0, 1 )$ and $( 0, 0 )$ lie on a circle for $k$ equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that, $( 1, 0 ) , ( 0, 1 ) , ( 0, 0 )$ lies on $X -$axis, $Y -$axis and on the origin respectively.

So, $( 2k, 3k )$ will lie on circle whose diameter is $AB$.

Equation of the circle will be given by,

$⇒ ( x - 1 ) ( x ) + ( y - 1 ) ( y ) = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} - x - y = 0 . . . \left(i\right)$

Using $( 2k, 3k )$ in equation \left(i\right)$,

$⇒ ( 2k{)}^{2} + ( 3k{)}^{2} - 2k - 3k = 0$

$⇒ 13k^{2} - 5k = 0$

$⇒ k = 0, k = $\dfrac{5}{13}

Hence, $k = \dfrac{5}{13}.$

$

questions.q: In the circle given below, let $OA = 1$ unit, $OB = 13$ unit and $PQ ⊥ OB$. Then, the area of the triangle $PQB$ (in square units) is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Since x-axis is normal to the circle at& $O$, and normal to the circle passes through its centre. So,~$OB$~is a diameter.

Now, perpendicular from centre of circle to chord bisects the chord, so~$PA = AQ = \lambda ( Let )$

Also, product of segments of chords in a circle is equal i.e.~$OA \cdot AB = AP \cdot AQ$

$⇒ 1 \cdot 12 = \lambda \cdot \lambda$

$⇒ \lambda = 2\sqrt{3}$~units

Now, area of~$\Delta PQB = \dfrac{1}{2} \times PQ \times AB = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2\lambda \times AB$

i.e.~$\Delta = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 4\sqrt{3} \times 12$~sq. units

$= 24\sqrt{3}$& sq. units

questions.q: Let ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ be the centres of the circles $x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x - 2y - 2 = 0$ and $x^{2} + y^{2} - 6x - 6y + 14 = 0$ respectively. If $P$ and $Q$ are the points of intersection of these circles, then the area (in sq. units) of the quadrilateral $P{C}_{1}Q{C}_{2}$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Equation of given circles are

${\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 1\right)}^{2} = 4$~and~${\left(x - 3\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 3\right)}^{2} = 4$.

Hence, ${C}_{1} \left(1, 1\right)$ and ${r}_{1} = 2$; ${C}_{2} \left(3, 3\right)$ and ${r}_{2} = 2$

$⇒ P{C}_{1} = P{C}_{2} = 2$

Now, by distance formula,

${C}_{1}{C}_{2} = \sqrt{\left(3 - 1\right)2 + \left(3 - 1\right)2} = \sqrt{{2}^{2} + {2}^{2}} = \sqrt{8}$

$⇒ P{C}_{1}^{2} + P{C}_{2}^{2} = {C}_{1}{C}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ ∠{C}_{1}P{C}_{2} = \dfrac{π}{2}$~(by converse of pythagoras~theorem in~$△ P{C}_{1}{C}_{2}$)

Hence, area of quadrilateral $P{C}_{1}Q{C}_{2} = 2 $\timesarea of~$△ P{C}_{1}{C}_{2} = 2 $\timesarea of~$△ Q{C}_{1}{C}_{2}$

$= 2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times2 \times2 = 4$

questions.q: The points of intersection of the line $ax + by = 0$, $( a \ne b )$ and the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x = 0$~are $A ( \alpha, 0 )$ and $B ( 1, \beta )$. The image of the circle with~$AB$~as a diameter in the line $x + y + 2 = 0$& is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The points of intersection of the line& $ax + by = 0, ( a \ne b )$~and the circle~$x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x = 0$~are~$A \left(\alpha,0\right)$~and~$B ( 1, \beta )$~then,

For point~$A \left(\alpha,0\right)$

$a ( \alpha ) +b ( 0 ) = 0 ⇒ \alpha =0$

And,~${α}^{2} - 2\alpha =0 ⇒ \alpha =0, 2$

For point~$B ( 1, \beta )$

$a + b\beta =0$

Or,~$\beta = \dfrac{- b}{a}$

And,~$1 + {β}^{2} - 2 = 0$

$⇒ \beta = \pm1$

$∵ a \ne b$~therefore,

Only possibility~$\alpha =0, \beta =1$

Points are~$A \left(0, 0\right)$~and~$B \left($1, 1\right)$

So the centre of the circle with diameter AB is~\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)~and radius~$r = $\dfrac{1}{2}

Now the image of~\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)~about the line~$x + y + 2 = 0$~is,

\dfrac{x - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = \dfrac{y - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = \dfrac{- 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + 2\right)}{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}

$⇒ $\dfrac{x - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = \dfrac{y - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = -$3$

$⇒$Centre of image circle is~ \left(- $\dfrac{5}{2}, - \dfrac{5}{2}\right)$

Equation of image circle

\left($x + \dfrac{5}{2}\right)2 + \left($y + \dfrac{5}{2}\right)2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$2$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} + 5x + 5y + 12 = 0$

$

questions.q: Let $C$ be the circle of minimum area touching the parabola $y=6-x^2$ and the lines $y=\sqrt{3}|x|$. Then, which one of the following points lies on the circle $C$ ?

questions.solution: Equation of circle $\mathrm{x}^2+(\mathrm{y}-(6-\mathrm{r}))^2=\mathrm{r}^2$ touches $\sqrt{3} \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}=0$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{p}=\mathrm{r} \\ & \frac{|0-(6-\mathrm{r})|}{2}=\mathrm{r} \\ & |\mathrm{r}-6|=2 \mathrm{r} \\ & \mathrm{r}=2 \end{aligned}$\therefore$ Circle $\mathrm{x}^2+(\mathrm{y}-4)^2=4(2,4)$ Satisfies this equation

questions.q: If the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} - 2gx + 6y - 19c = 0, g, c \in \mathbb{R}$~passes through the point  \left(6, 1\right)$ and its centre lies on the line $x - 2cy = 8$, then the length of intercept made by the circle on $x$-axis is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given circle& $x^{2} + y^{2} - 2gx + 6y - 19c = 0$

Also given circle passes through~ \left(6, 1\right)$

So,~$12g + 19c = 43 ⋯ \left(1\right)$

And centre~ \left(g, - 3\right)$~lies on~$x - 2cy = 8$,

So,~$g + 6c = 8 \ldots \left(2\right)$

On solving~equation~ \left($1\right)$~and~ \left(2\right)$~we get,~$c = 1$~and~$g = 2$

Now equation~of circle will be, $x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 6y - 19 = 0$

Now length of intercept on~$x$-axis is given by~$= 2\sqrt{g^{2} - C} =$==2\sqrt{{2}^{2} + 19} =$==2\sqrt{23}$

$

questions.q: Let $C$~be the centre of the circle~$x^{2} + y^{2} - x + 2y = \dfrac{11}{4}$~and $P$~be a point on the circle. A line passes through the point $C$, makes an angle of $\dfrac{π}{4}$ with the line $CP$ and intersects the circle at the points $Q$~and $R$. Then the area of the triangle $PQR$ (in~${unit}^{2}$) is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$x^{2} + y^{2} - x + 2y = \dfrac{11}{4}$

On rearranging terms we get,

$⇒ \left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)2 + \left(y + 1\right)2 = \left(2\right)2$

Now given in~$∆ PQR$,~$∠ PCR = \dfrac{π}{4}$~so~$∠ PQR = 22\dfrac{1}{2}$~by circle property, radius is~$2$~so~$RC = QC = 2$

Now,~$PR = QRsin22\dfrac{1}{2}= 4sin\dfrac{π}{8}$

And~$PQ = QRcos22\dfrac{1}{2} = 4\cos 22\dfrac{1}{2}$

Now area of~$\Delta PQR = \dfrac{1}{2}PR \times PQ$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \lleft(4sin\dfrac{π}{8})\llleft(4cos\dfrac{π}{8})

$= 4 $\times \left(2sin\dfrac{π}}{8}cos\dfrac{π}{8}\right)$

=4sin\dfrac{π}{4} = \dfrac{4}{2} ==2\sqrt{2}$

$

questions.q: Three circles of radii $a, b, c,  \left(a < b < c\right)$ touch each other externally. If they have $x$-axis as a common tangent, then:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$LM = PN = \sqrt{\left(a + b\right)2 - \left(b - a\right)2} = 2\sqrt{ab}$

$NQ = MS = \sqrt{\left(a + c\right)2 - \left(c - a\right)2} = 2\sqrt{ac}$

$PQ = ST = \sqrt{\left(b + c\right)2 - \left(c - b\right)2} = 2\sqrt{bc}$

$∵PQ = PN + NQ$

$⇒ 2\sqrt{bc} = 2\sqrt{ab} + 2\sqrt{ac}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{b}} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{c}}$

questions.q: If a variable line& $3x + 4y - \lambda = 0$ is such that the two circles $x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x - 2y + 1 = 0$ and $x^{2} + y^{2} - 18x - 2y + 78 = 0$ are on its opposite sides, then the set of all values of $\lambda$ is the interval :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given circles& $x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x - 2y + 1 = 0 ⇒ \left(x - 1\right)2 + \left(y - 1\right)2 = {1}^{2}$~and

$x^{2} + y^{2} - 18x - 2y + 78 = 0 ⇒ \left(x - 9\right)2 + \left(y - 1\right)2 = {2}^{2}$

Thus, centers of two circles are~ \left(1, 1\right) \text{ and } \left(9, 1\right)$~and radii are~$1 \text{ and } 2$~respectively.

Since, center~of circles are on the opposite side of line~$3x + 4y - \lambda = 0$.

$⇒ \left($3 + 4 - \lambda\right)\left($27 + 4 - \lambda\right) < 0$

$⇒ \left(7 - \lambda\right) \left(31 - \lambda\right) < 0$

$⇒ \lambda \in \left(7, 31\right) \ldots \ldots . \left(i\right)$

Since, circles should not intersect given line.

Hence,~\left|\dfrac{7 - \lambda}{{3}^{2} + {4}^{2}}\right| \ge 1 \text{ and } \left|\dfrac{31 - \lambda}{{3}^{2} + {4}^{2}}\right| \ge 2$

$⇒ \left|7 - \lambda\right| \ge 5 \text{ and } \left|31 - \lambda\right| ≥ 10$

$⇒ \lambda ≤ 2$~or~$\lambda ≥ 12 \ldots \ldots . \left(ii\right)$

and $\lambda ≤ 21$~or~$\lambda ≥ 41 \ldots \ldots . \left(iii\right)$

Thus,~$\lambda \in \left(i\right) \cap \left($ii\right) \cap \left($iii\right)$

$⇒ \lambda \in \left[$12,21\right]$

$

questions.q: The set of all values of $a^{2}$~for which the line $x + y = 0$~bisects two distinct chords drawn from a point $P \left(\dfrac{1 + a}{2}, \dfrac{1 - a}{2}\right) on the circle $2x^{2} + 2y^{2} - ( 1 + a ) x - ( 1 - a ) y = 0$, is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The line& $y = - x$~bisect the chord~$PQ$

If~ \left(\lambda, - \lambda\right)$~is~the mid-point of the chord~$PQ$~then,

$Q ( 2\lambda - \alpha, - 2\lambda - \beta )$

Given circle~$2x^{2} + 2y^{2} - ( 1 + a ) x - ( 1 - a ) y = 0$

Or,~$x^{2} + y^{2} - \left(\dfrac{1 + a}{2}\right)x - \left(\dfrac{1 - a}{2}\right)y = 0$

Let~$\dfrac{1 + a}{2} = \alpha, \dfrac{1 - a}{2} = \beta$

The circle equation will be,

$x^{2} + y^{2} - \alphax - \betay = 0$

Point $Q$ will lie on the circle,

$( 2\lambda - \alpha{)}^{2} + ( - 2\lambda - \beta{)}^{2} - \alpha ( 2\lambda - \alpha ) - \beta ( - 2\lambda - \beta ) = 0$

$⇒ 4{λ}^{2} + 3\lambda ( \beta - \alpha ) + \left({α}^{2} + {β}^{2}\right) = 0$

So, quadratic in~$\lambda$~should have~$D > 0$

$⇒ 9 ( \beta - \alpha{)}^{2} - 4 ( 4 ) \left({α}^{2} + {β}^{2}\right) > 0$

Put the value of~$\alpha$~and~$\beta$~we get,

$⇒ 9a^{2} - 16\left(\dfrac{1 + a^{2}}{2}\right) > 0$

$⇒ a^{2} > 8$

$

questions.q: Let a circle passing through $(2,0)$ have its centre at the point $(h, k)$. Let  \left(x_c, y_c\right)$ be the point of intersection of the lines $3 x+5 y=1$ and $(2+c) x+5 c^2 y=1$. questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & (2+c) x+5 c^2\left(\frac{1-3 x}{5}\right)=1 \\ & x=\frac{1-c^2}{2+c-3 c^2}, y=\frac{1-3 x}{5}=\frac{c-1}{5\left(2+c-3 c^2\right)} \\ & h=\lim _{c \rightarrow 1} \frac{(1-c)(1+c)}{(1-c)(2+3 c)}=\frac{2}{5} \\ & K=\lim _{c \rightarrow 1} \frac{c-1}{-5(c-1)(3 c+2)}=-\frac{1}{25} \\ & \operatorname{Centre}\left(\frac{2}{25},-\frac{1}{25}\right)\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & r=\sqrt{\left(2-\frac{2}{5}\right)^2+\left(0-\frac{1}{25}\right)^2}=\sqrt{\frac{64}{25}+\frac{1}{625}} \\ & r=\frac{\sqrt{161}}{25} \\ & \left(x-\frac{2}{5}\right)^2+\left(y+\frac{1}{25}\right)^2=\frac{161}{125} \\ & \Rightarrow 25 x^2+25 y^2-20 x+2 y-60=0\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: If the circles $x^{2} + y^{2} - 16x - 20y + 164 = r^{2}$ and ${( x - 4 )}^{2} + {\left(y - 7\right)}^{2} = 36$ intersect at two distinct points, then:

As we know, if two circles intersect each other, then

\left|{r}_{1} - {r}_{2}\right| < {C}_{1}{C}_{2} < {r}_{1} + {r}_{2}$ ........(i)

Now for the first circle ${C}_{1} \left(8, 10\right)$ and ${r}_{1} = r$

For the second circle ${C}_{2} \left(4, 7\right)$ and ${r}_{2} = 6$

From (i)

\left|r - 6\right| < 5 < r + 6$

$⇒ \left|r - 6\right| < 5 . . . \left(ii\right)$~&~$5 < r + 6 . . . \left(iii\right)\left\{\left|r - 6\right| = \left\{
r - 6, r \ge 6
6 - r, r < 6
\right\right\}$

from~ \left(iii\right)$~$r > - 1 . . . \left(iv\right)$

from~ \left(ii\right)$~

when~$- 1 < r < 6$~then~$6 - r < 5 ⇒ 1 < r . . . \left(v\right)$

when~$r ≥ 6 ⇒ r - 6 < 5 ⇒ r < 11 . . . \left($vi\right)$

from~ \left(iv\right), \left($v\right), \left(vi\right)$~we get

$⇒ r \in \left($1, 11\right)$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & C_1 C_2=\sqrt{(2+2)^2+(5-2)^2} \\ & =\sqrt{16+9} \\ & =5 \\ & r+2 \gt 5 \\ & r \gt 3 \\ & r \lt 5+2 \\ & r \lt 7 \\ & \therefore \alpha=3, \beta=7 \\ & 3 \beta-2 \alpha=3(7)-2(3)=21-6=15\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let& $C$ be a circle passing through the points $A  \left(2, - 1\right)$~and $B  \left(3, 4\right)$. The line segment $AB$~is not a diameter of $C$. If $r$~is the radius of $C$ and its centre lies on the circle \left(x - 5\right)2 + \left(y - 1\right)2 = \dfrac{13}{2},$then $r^{2}$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Equation of line joining& $AB$~is~

$y + 1 = 5 \left(x - 2\right)$

i.e.~$5x - y - 11 = 0$~

Also~$AB = $\sqrt{\left(3 - 2\right)2 + \left(4 + 1\right)2} = \sqrt{26}

$r$~is the radius of the circle~$C$

For the circle~ \left(x - 5\right)2 + \left($y - 1\right)2 = $\dfrac{13}{2}

centre is~\left($5, 1\right)$~and radius~$R = $\sqrt{\dfrac{13}{2}}

Equation of perpendicular bisector of~$AB$~will be~$y - 1 = - $\dfrac{1}{5}\left($x - 5\right) ⇒ x + 5y - 10 = 0$

Solving this equation of line with~\left($x - 5\right)2 + \left(y - 1\right)2 = \dfrac{13}{2},$we get~

$M$~as~\left(\dfrac{5}{2}, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$~

So~$M$~lies on the line joining~$AB$.

Now~$r^{2} = CM^{2} + AM^{2}$

$= \left(2 \times \sqrt{\dfrac{13}{2}}\right)2 + \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{13}{2}}\right)2$

$r^{2} = \dfrac{65}{2}$

$

questions.q: Consider a circle ${C}_{1}: x{ }^{2} + y^{2} – 4x – 2y = \alpha – 5 .$ Let its mirror image in the line $y = 2x + 1$ be another circle ${C}_{2}: 5x^{2} + 5y^{2} – 10fx – 10gy + 36 = 0 .$~ Let~$r$ be the radius of ${C}_{2}$ . Then $\alpha + r$ is equal to ________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${C}_{1}: {x}_{2} + {y}_{2} – 4x – 2y + \left(5 – \alpha\right) =0$

So, its centre will be,~${O}_{1} = \left(2, 1\right)$~and~radius~=\sqrt{\alpha}

And~${C}_{2}: 5x^{2} + 5y^{2} – 10fx – 10gy + 36 = 0$

$⇒ {C}_{2}: x^{2} + y^{2} – 2fx – 2gy + $\dfrac{36}{5} =$0$

So, Centre ${O}_{2} = \left(f, g\right)$~and radius $r = \sqrt{f^{2} + g^{2} - \dfrac{36}{5}}$

Also given~${O}_{2}$ is reflection of ${O}_{1}$ in $2x – y + 1 = 0$, so image formula we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{f - 2}{2} = \dfrac{g - 1}{- 1} = -2 \cdot \left(\dfrac{2 \times 2 - 1 + 1}{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2}}\right)$

$⇒ f = \dfrac{- 6}{5}$~and~$g = \dfrac{13}{5}$

So, radius~$r = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{- 6}{5}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{13}{5}\right)2 - \dfrac{36}{5}} = \dfrac{25}{5} =1$

$⇒ r = 1$and~$\alpha =1$~as they both are same radius circle,

Hence,~$r + \alpha =2.

$

questions.q: If the curves, $x^{2} - 6x + y^{2} + 8 = 0$ and $x^{2} - 8y + y^{2} + 16 - k = 0,  \left(k > 0\right)$ touch each other at a point, then the largest value of $k is ____________.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
If general equation of circle is& $x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$~then its center is~ \left(- g, - f\right)$~and radius is~$\sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}$

Two circles touches each other if ${C}_{1}{C}_{2} = \left|{r}_{1} \pm {r}_{2}\right|$

Distance between ${C}_{2}\left(3, 0\right)and{C}_{1}\left($0, 4\right)$ is either $\sqrt{k} ++$1or\left|$\sqrt{k} -$1\right|$

${C}_{1}{C}_{2} = $\sqrt{\left(3 - 0\right)2 + \left(0 - 4\right)2} =$5$

$⇒ $\sqrt{k} +$1 = 5$or~\left|$\sqrt{k} +$1\right| = 5$

$⇒ k = 16$~or~$k = 36$

$⇒$~Maximum value of $k$ is $36$.
